items.title: Binary residue carrier and operations
items.statement_or_definition:
Set
$$
\mathbb F_2:=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z=\{[0]_2,[1]_2\},
$$
with addition and multiplication induced by the quotient operations
$$
[r]_2+[s]_2=[r+s]_2,\qquad [r]_2[s]_2=[rs]_2
$$
from [[def-addition-and-multiplication-modulo-n]]. This item fixes the two residue classes and their operations. It does not assert the field axioms; those must be established separately before an argument uses field properties.
proof_obligations: Verify the two residues are distinct and both quotient operations close on the two-element carrier; do not assert field laws here.

items.title: Binary dot product as parity
items.statement_or_definition:
For $n\ge0$ and $a,x\in\{0,1\}^{n}$, define the one-bit **binary dot product**
$$
a\cdot x:=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{n-1}(a_i\land x_i),
$$
where $\land$ is Boolean conjunction and $\bigoplus$ is the left-to-right fold of XOR, with empty fold $0$. It is the parity of the number of coordinates where both bits are $1$. Under the quotient operations of [[def-qa-binary-field-f2]], this bit represents the sum $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}[a_i]_2[x_i]_2$ in $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$; the equality uses only the operation definitions, not the field axioms.
proof_obligations: Verify Boolean conjunction is multiplication on bits and the left-to-right XOR fold represents the quotient sum, including the empty fold.

items.title: Reversible binary dot-product query
items.statement_or_definition:
**Input:** An integer $n\ge0$, ordered $n$-bit registers $|a\rangle,|x\rangle$, a one-bit target $|z\rangle$, and one distinct clean work bit $r=0$.

**Output:** The reversible map
$$
|a\rangle|x\rangle|z\rangle|0\rangle_r\longmapsto|a\rangle|x\rangle|z\oplus(a\cdot x)\rangle|0\rangle_r.
$$

**Gate model:** Use an operation model whose declared finite nonoracle gate alphabet contains and permits Toffoli and CNOT as callable gates; each listed occurrence counts once under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. This procedure makes no black-box oracle call.

**Instructions:** For $i=0,1,\ldots,n-1$, apply Toffoli with controls $a_i,x_i$ and target $r$. Apply CNOT from $r$ to $z$. Then apply those same Toffoli gates in reverse order, from $i=n-1$ down to $0$. All gates act on the ordered computational-basis registers of [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]; their basis actions are fixed in [[def-qc-toffoli-and-fredkin]] and [[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]]. For $n=0$, the forward and reverse loops are empty and the XOR fold is $0$.

The procedure uses $2n$ Toffoli occurrences and one CNOT occurrence, with one clean work bit. It has no failure branch.
proof_obligations: State the ordered inputs, target, clean work, exact forward/copy/reverse instructions, output, cost, and n=0 behavior.

items.title: Reversible binary dot product: correctness and exact cost
items.statement_or_definition:
For every $n\ge0$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-reversible-binary-dot-product]] maps every computational-basis input to
$$
|a\rangle|x\rangle|z\rangle|0\rangle_r\longmapsto|a\rangle|x\rangle|z\oplus(a\cdot x)\rangle|0\rangle_r.
$$
It therefore implements the same linear map on superpositions. Its exact cost is $2n$ Toffoli gates, one CNOT, and one clean work bit; it has no failure branch.
proof_obligations: Track the forward parity invariant, target toggle, reverse cleanup, linear extension, exact counts, and empty-input boundary.

items.title: Standard bit-flip query convention
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $a,b\ge 0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}^{b}$ be a total function. The **standard bit-flip query** for $f$ is the coherent XOR action
$$
U_f|x\rangle|y\rangle=|x\rangle|y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered $a$-bit address register followed by the ordered $b$-bit target register. Here $\oplus$ is componentwise addition modulo two, and words label the ordered computational basis as in [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] and [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]. The address is unchanged. One invocation is one query under [[def-qa-promise-query-instance]]; its query cost is separate from elementary gate cost.

The map is an involution and is unitary by [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. No injectivity of $f$ is assumed.
proof_obligations: State the total-function domain, address and target widths, register order, XOR action, and one-call query charge.

items.title: Binary phase-query convention
items.statement_or_definition:
For a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}$, the **phase query** is the linear operator on the address register defined on its ordered computational basis by
$$
P_f|x\rangle=(-1)^{f(x)}|x\rangle.
$$
This definition supplies uncontrolled access only. Controlled access to $P_f$ is a separate promise and is not implied by an uncontrolled call.
proof_obligations: Check the phase action is unitary and involutive on the full address register.

items.title: Phase kickback from the standard bit query
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}$ be a total Boolean function. If the one-bit target of its standard query is prepared in
$$
|-\rangle:=\frac{|0\rangle-|1\rangle}{\sqrt2},
$$
then one standard query acts on every address basis vector by
$$
U_f(|x\rangle|-\rangle)=(-1)^{f(x)}|x\rangle|-\rangle.
$$
Thus the address acquires exactly the phase query $P_f$, while the target returns unchanged. The same identity holds for every address superposition.
proof_obligations: Check both Boolean values on the target basis and extend the exact identity to arbitrary finite address superpositions.

items.title: Compute-copy-uncompute yields a clean coherent function query
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}^{b}$ be total. Suppose a finite nonoracle gate circuit $V$ preserves the address and, from zero value and workspace registers, computes
$$
V|x\rangle|0^b\rangle|0^w\rangle=|x\rangle|f(x)\rangle|0^w\rangle
$$
for every $x$, with gate count $G$. Suppose its exact inverse circuit is available with the same gate count and acts only on the address, value, and workspace registers. Applying $V$, copying the $b$ output bits to a fresh target by $b$ CNOTs, and applying $V^{-1}$ implements the standard query, restores the value and workspace registers to zero, and uses exactly $2G+b$ gate occurrences. Any query calls in a different implementation must be charged separately.

For a finite Boolean DAG with $S$ noninput nodes, $E$ input-port uses counted with multiplicity, and $b$ ordered output ports, the current QC10 reversible-embedding construction itself already implements the clean XOR query. Its local cost theorem gives at most $6S+4E+b$ gates and $S+E$ clean work bits. Thus its size is $O(S+E+b)$, and is $O(S+b)$ when $E=O(S)$, as for the stated bounded-fan-in graphs. No depth bound is inferred from the classical Boolean DAG.
proof_obligations: Prove the generic clean-evaluator sequence and exact 2G+b count; use the actual QC10 complete-query bound without charging its copy/uncompute twice.

items.title: A constant phase query is invisible alone and relative under control
items.statement_or_definition: Let $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}$ be constant with value $c\in\{0,1\}$. Its phase query is $P_f=(-1)^cI$. A standalone call therefore leaves every pure-state measurement law unchanged. If the model explicitly grants controlled phase-query access, the two constant cases are distinguishable: on address $|0^a\rangle$ and control $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, control of $P_f$ returns $|+\rangle|0^a\rangle$ when $c=0$ and $|-\rangle|0^a\rangle$ when $c=1$. Measuring the control in the $\{|+\rangle,|-\rangle\}$ basis distinguishes them with certainty. No controlled access is inferred from a bare phase-query call.
proof_obligations: Verify constant phase on every basis vector, standalone invariance, explicit controlled access, and the finite distinguishing measurement.

items.title: One standard query implements one phase query
items.statement_or_definition: Let $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}$ be total. Starting a target qubit in $|0\rangle$, apply $X$ and then $H$, and make one standard bit query. Since $HX|0\rangle=|-\rangle$, phase kickback implements $P_f$ on the address and returns the target to $|-\rangle$. This conversion uses one query plus exactly two nonoracle one-qubit gates; the target preparation is explicit and assumes no preprepared state or generic amplitude loading.
proof_obligations: Verify the explicit preparation H X |0> = |-> and charge the one oracle call separately from the two preparation gates.

items.title: Controlled phase access implements a standard bit query
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{a}\to\{0,1\}$ be total. Assume the operation model explicitly supplies the controlled phase call
$$
C(P_f)=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\0&P_f\end{pmatrix}
$$
with the output qubit as the first, control register. On address $|x\rangle$ and output $|y\rangle$, apply $H$ to the output, make one controlled phase call, and apply $H$ again. The result is $|x\rangle|y\oplus f(x)\rangle$, so this implements one standard query with one controlled phase call and two nonoracle $H$ gates. Bare uncontrolled $P_f$ access does not satisfy the stated access hypothesis.
proof_obligations: Verify output control values 0 and 1, the H diag(1,-1) H identity, and the explicit controlled-access hypothesis.

title: Reversible Arithmetic and Oracle Conversion — Examples

items.title: Oracle conversion and uncomputation examples
items.statement_or_definition: For the one-bit function $f(x)=x$, compute the standard XOR query with a clean work bit, copy its value to the target, and uncompute the work. On input address $|+\rangle$, target $|-\rangle$, and work $|0\rangle$, the address becomes $|-\rangle$ and the work returns to zero; a final Hadamard on the address yields outcome $1$ with certainty. For the two-bit dot product, take $a=11$, $x=10$, and target $z=0$. The reversible Toffoli circuit outputs target $1$ and resets its work bit. If the one-bit circuit omits its final uncomputation, residual address-dependent work makes the same final address measurement uniform instead of deterministic. Finally, a constant-one phase query has no standalone measurement effect, but its controlled call changes a control $|+\rangle$ to $|-\rangle$.
proof_obligations: Check the one-bit clean query, two-bit dot product, dirty-work interference failure, and controlled constant-phase calculation directly.
